The ball leaves the floor at x = 0 moving 3.01 m/s forward and 8.72 m/s up. It peaks at 3.99 m around 0.89 s and comes down through the rim at 1.33 s, 8 cm from its centre. It touches nothing on the way in: it misses the front rim by 6 cm and the backboard's lower edge by 12 cm. It lands near x = 5.3 m at 1.78 s and bounces off the floor and the support pole. It comes to rest by 2.35 s, then creeps a few centimetres and lightly touches the pole again at 5.20 s.

The brief asks only for the shot, so this works. One thing is unrealistic: the floor bounce is very dead. The ball comes down at about 8.4 m/s and rebounds at well under 1 m/s, whereas a real basketball would bounce much higher. That happens after the part the brief describes, so I'm leaving it.
